title: Descriptive Statistics (General Statistics)
description: The first statistics course, STA 111/114: General Statistics: data types, sources and measurement scales, data presentation, measures of centre, variability, relative position and shape, confidence intervals for means and proportions, hypothesis testing, and correlation and regression. Built from the STA 114 lectures of Dr O. Otekunrin, Prof. A. A. Adepoju and Dr A. A. Ogunde (2024/25), the course outline and lecture summary, with the 2025 test.

topics.title: Data: Types, Sources, Quality and Measurement Scales
topics.summary: Statistics is the science of collecting, organising, analysing and interpreting data. Data are qualitative or quantitative, come from primary or secondary sources, must be of good quality, and are measured on nominal, ordinal, interval or ratio scales.
subtopics: What statistics is; descriptive and inferential statistics
Qualitative and quantitative; discrete and continuous
Sources of data and methods of collection
Nominal, ordinal, interval and ratio scales

topics.title: Presentation of Data
topics.summary: Data are presented in tables and diagrams to make them easier to understand. Frequency distributions group data into classes, and charts such as bar charts, pie charts, histograms, frequency polygons and stem-and-leaf displays show their pattern.
subtopics: Class limits, boundaries, marks and widths
Line, bar, pictogram and pie charts
Histograms, frequency polygons, ogives and stem-and-leaf

topics.title: Measures of Centre
topics.summary: Measures of centre (location) locate where data cluster: the arithmetic, geometric and harmonic means, the median and the mode. Each has formulas for ungrouped and grouped data and suits different kinds of data.
subtopics: Arithmetic mean: ungrouped, frequency and grouped data
Median of ungrouped and grouped data
Mode and the grouped-data mode formula

topics.title: Measures of Variability and the Normal Rules
topics.summary: Measures of variability show how spread out data are: the range, variance, standard deviation and coefficient of variation. The empirical rule describes bell-shaped data, and Chebyshev's rule bounds any data set.

topics.title: Relative Position, Skewness and Kurtosis
topics.summary: Quartiles, deciles and percentiles locate values within ordered data, z-scores standardise them, and the interquartile range detects outliers. Skewness and kurtosis describe the shape of a distribution.
subtopics: Interquartile range and the five-number summary
Detecting outliers with the 1.5 IQR rule

topics.title: Confidence Intervals
topics.summary: A confidence interval gives a range of plausible values for a population parameter. STA 111 builds intervals for one mean, two means, one proportion and two proportions, using z for large samples and t for small ones.
subtopics: Point and interval estimates; margin of error
Interval for one mean, σ known or n large
Interval for the difference of two means

topics.title: Hypothesis Testing, Correlation and Regression
topics.summary: A hypothesis test decides between a null and an alternative hypothesis using a test statistic and a critical value. Correlation measures the strength of a linear relationship, while regression predicts one variable from another.
subtopics: Null and alternative hypotheses; Type I and II errors
Steps of a test; critical values and decisions
Tests for one mean and two means
Scatter diagrams and Pearson's correlation r
